title: Directed ring colimits of separably closed fields
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty small directed poset and $(k_i,v_{ij})_{i\le j}$ a direct system of fields and unital field homomorphisms. Suppose that each $k_i$ is separably closed [def-pc-separably-closed]. Let $k$ be a field and $(\rho_i:k_i\to k)$ a compatible family exhibiting $k$ as the colimit of this diagram in commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Then $k$ is separably closed: every nonconstant separable polynomial $p\in k[T]$ [def-pc-separable-polynomial] has a root in $k$. The extensions between stages need not be algebraic.

source.place: Tag 04GI, lemma-colimit-henselian, proof: sentence that the colimit of separably algebraically closed residue fields is separably algebraically closed.

proof.text: Let p be a separable polynomial over k. The directed nonempty poset I is filtered, and the forgetful functor from commutative rings preserves filtered colimits. By clause (1) of [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise], choose a stage representative of each coefficient indexed by the finite support of p, using Concrete.isColimit_exists_rep for the supplied colimit cocone.

By directedness a finite set of stage indices has a common upper bound i (Finset.exists_le, also for empty support since I is nonempty). Transport the coefficient representatives to stage i. Cocone naturality identifies their images with the coefficients of p; outside the support use the zero element. Polynomial.mem_map_range now gives q over the stage with q.map(rho_i) = p. This uses only finite-element descent, not descent of any equations.

Give the stage its field structure from hF i. By [def-pc-separable-polynomial] and Polynomial.separable_map, separability of q.map(rho_i) = p implies separability of q. Reflection of separability along a field map is valid even for transcendental extensions; no Bezout identity needs to descend.

By [def-pc-separably-closed], the separable stage polynomial q splits. Map its splitting along rho_i using Polynomial.Splits.map. Its image is p, so every separable polynomial over k splits. This is precisely the Mathlib class IsSepClosed k, equivalent to the root formulation of the statement. Zero and constant polynomials are included automatically.
